function.description: Calculates the price for a service based on the geolocation of the customer, ensuring a minimum price threshold is met. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

geolocation.description: The geolocation of the customer in the format of 'Latitude, Longitude', such as '34.0522, -118.2437'.

base_price.description: The base price for the service before location-based adjustments. This is a float type value.

minimum_price.description: The minimum price to charge regardless of the customer's location. This is a float type value.

location_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the base price based on customer's geolocation. A higher multiplier indicates a more expensive area. This is a float type value.

message.content:
### Quick Take‑away  
**Price your SaaS around $129–$139 per filing for a single‑use plan and **$179–$199** for an annual “unlimited” plan—slightly above the mid‑tier competitor ($149) but below the high‑price competitor ($249). Add optional add‑ons (priority processing, audit protection, extra storage) so you can upsell without diluting core value.  

Below is a deeper dive into why this range works and how to fine‑tune it once you launch.

---

## 1️⃣ Understand Your Cost & Margin Baseline  

| Item | Typical % of Revenue |
|------|---------------------|
| Direct labor / tech ops | 20–30% |
| Customer acquisition (CAC) | 25–35% |
| Support/maintenance | 10–15% |
| Platform hosting & infra | 5–8% |

Assuming a gross margin goal of ~55%, you’ll want revenue per user roughly twice the sum of direct + CAC. That’s why most SaaS firms aim for ~$120–140 per transaction when they’re targeting small‑to‑mid sized businesses.

> *Tip:* Run a quick break‑even calculator using your actual numbers – if your CAC is lower than industry averages, you could push the price up slightly.

---

## 2️⃣ Position Yourself Between Competitors  

| Feature | Competitor A | Competitor B | Our Suggested Price Point |
|---------|--------------|-------------|---------------------------|
| One‑time filing | $99 | $149 | **$129–$139** |
| Unlimited yearly plan | $149 | $249 | **$179–$199** |
| Renewal frequency | Annual | Annual | Annual (no auto‑renew at sign‑up) |
| Extra perks | Basic | Premium | Tiered add‑ons (audit shield, priority queue, API access) |

*Why this middle ground?*

- **Perceived Value:** You’re closer to the low‑priced option, which signals affordability, yet still command premium over the cheapest competitor because you offer better reliability/support.
- **Margin Cushion:** Slightly higher than the lowest competitor gives room for marketing spend while staying attractive against the highest priced rival.
- **Competitive Differentiation:** By offering a clear upgrade path from a single filing to an unlimited plan, you create natural upselling opportunities.

---

## 3️⃣ Build a Simple Pricing Matrix  

```
+-----------------------------------+
| Plan          | Monthly | Yearly   |
+-----------------------------------+
| Single Filing | $129    | N/A      |
| Unlimited     | $179/mo | $199/yr  |
+-----------------------------------+

Add‑Ons:
• Priority Queue (+$19/month)
• Audit Shield (+$29/year)
• Dedicated Account Manager (+$49/month)
```

- **Monthly vs. Yearly:** Offer both options but make the yearly cheaper overall (e.g., $199 instead of $12×$179 ≈ $2149). This encourages longer commitments without locking users into automatic renewal.
- **Bundled Discounts:** If someone signs up for the unlimited plan plus two add‑ons, provide a 10% bundle discount. Bundles increase average order size and lock-in.

---

## 4️⃣ Test & Iterate Quickly  

| Phase | Action | KPI |
|-------|--------|-----|
| Launch | Soft‑launch to early adopters at $119 single + $169 unlimited | Conversion rate, churn |
| Feedback | Survey satisfaction after first filing | Net Promoter Score (NPS) |
| Adjust | Raise single to $129 if churn < 5%; raise unlimited to $189 if churn > 10% | Churn, ARPU |

Use A/B testing on landing pages and email campaigns to see whether people prefer monthly or yearly billing. Track cohort retention across pricing tiers.

---

## 5️⃣ Leverage Psychological Anchoring  

- **Anchor High → Anchor Low:** Show the “old price” next to the new price (“Was $159”). Even though you don’t have a legacy price, you can anchor against the $149 competitor.
- **Scarcity Tactics:** Limited‑time introductory rates (first 100 signups get $109 single) drive urgency.
- **Tier Naming:** Instead of generic names, call them “Starter,” “Pro,” and “Enterprise.” Names evoke status and help justify incremental price differences.

---

## 6️⃣ Differentiate Beyond Price  

Even if you match the competition on price, you win through:

| Area | What to Do |
|------|------------|
| Speed | Guarantee same‑day filing turnaround within 24 hrs. |
| Compliance | Real‑time alerts for regulatory changes. |
| Integration | Native connectors to popular accounting software. |
| UX | Intuitive UI that reduces training time. |
| Trust | Transparent audit trail, data encryption, SOC 2 compliant. |

These differentiators allow you to maintain a premium perception even if the headline price isn’t dramatically higher.

---

## 7️⃣ Final Recommendation Snapshot  

| Service Type | Suggested Price | Rationale |
|--------------|-----------------|-----------|
| One‑Time Filing | **$129** | Midway between $99 and $149; positions us as affordable yet reliable. |
| Unlimited Annual Subscription | **$179** | Competitive versus $149/$249; includes all filings + basic add‑on bundles. |
| Optional Add‑On Bundle | Up to **$229** (incl. 10% off) | Upsells for power users; keeps ARPU healthy. |

Keep monitoring key metrics (CAC, LTV, churn) and stay ready to shift the price point upward if you consistently outperform the $149 benchmark in terms of feature set and support quality.

---

### Bottom Line  
Set a baseline that sits comfortably between your rivals’ offerings, then layer in strategic add‑ons and psychological tactics to maximize adoption and lifetime value. With continuous feedback loops and agile pricing experiments, you’ll find the sweet spot that balances profitability with market share growth.
